Below is a quick summary of what’s happening, why it’s broken, and the minimal change needed to make empty‐string literals `''` highlight correctly in the Smalltalk grammar.

1. Bug scenario & root cause  
   • In Prism’s Smalltalk mode the string rule is defined as:  
     ```js
     'string': /'(?:''|[^'])+'/,
     ```  
     The `+` quantifier there means “at least one occurrence of either `''` or any non-quote character.” As a result, a standalone empty string `''` (which has zero characters inside) doesn’t match this pattern, so it never gets tokenized as a string.  
   • Browsers like Rouge handle this by using `*` (zero or more) instead of `+`. We need to do the same.

2. Patch  
   Change the `+` to `*` in the string rule. This will allow zero-length content between the quotes, i.e. `''`.

```javascript
### components/prism-smalltalk.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
    'string': /\'(?:\'\'|[^\'])+\'/,
=======
    'string': /\'(?:\'\'|[^\'])*\'/,
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

With that one‐line change, empty strings (`''`) will now be recognized and highlighted properly.

is being tokenized as

  – a string starting at the first quote,  
  – then “nothing” inside (because the regexp doesn’t allow an empty match),  
  – then the second quote is never seen as the end of that string, so everything that follows is swept into the “string” token until the next lone quote is found.

In our Prism grammar for Smalltalk (`components/prism-smalltalk.js`), the culprit is this line:

    'string': /'(?:''|[^'])+'/,

the `+` requires at least one inner token (`''` or a non-quote), so `''` (an empty string) fails to match.  We need to allow zero repetitions, i.e. change the `+` to `*`.

Here is the single *SEARCH/REPLACE* patch.  We include three lines of context to make the search robust:

```javascript
### components/prism-smalltalk.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
    'comment': /"(?:""|[^"])+"/,
```
